feature: Describe what to create makes it, and Ask works with nothing open
summary: Type a picture into the New window's Describe field and Create opens a new image and Ask draws it there, with its row in the Agent area. In an empty window the title bar Ask, Edit > Ask… and Command K are ready and do the same.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Ask needs its local model running, as it does everywhere else today.

try.do: Press Command N, type "a sunset over the sea" into Describe what to create.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Return. A new 1440 by 1024 image opens, the New window closes, and Ask draws the sunset with a Drew a sunset over the sea row.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z once: the drawing goes, the blank picture stays.
Press Command N, type "a video of waves on a beach" and press Create: it says Ask can't make videos yet and keeps your words.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In a window with nothing open (its card says Drop an image here), click Ask in the title bar and ask "measure this": it says Nothing is open yet.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In the same window ask "a lighthouse at night, 800 x 600": the window becomes an 800 by 600 picture with the lighthouse drawn.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In the New window press Command K: the cursor goes into Describe what to create.

evaluate: Is Return in the Describe field making the picture (and not a blank New Image) what you expect?
Should a request with no size or shape take the size picked in the list below the field (Desktop by default), as it does now?
Do the two one-line answers (Ask can't make videos yet. / Nothing is open yet.) say enough, or should they point at what to do next?
Does the Ask button alone in an empty window's title bar read as ready, next to the card?
rough: The sunset was drawn as a smaller picture in the middle of the white canvas rather than filling it, though the canvas was made just for it; the lighthouse did fill its canvas. That is how Ask places a drawing, folded into ask-on-the-local-model-makes-results-that-look-f.

What kind of request it is (a picture, a video, about something already open) is read from the words: working verbs at the start (measure, crop, find), words pointing at something open (this, the screenshot), and words naming time (video, animated). A request phrased oddly can land on the wrong side; the answer then says so and keeps the words.

A request names its shape by a size (800 x 600) or a format (a banner, a poster, a square image, portrait orientation); otherwise it takes the size picked in the New window. Ask can still turn the blank picture into an icon frame, as it does on any blank picture.
The New window draws its own title bar, so it has no Ask button: Edit > Ask… and Command K put the cursor in its Describe field instead.
No mock covers Ask in an empty window or the one-line answers.
The New window's prompt bar matches ui-entry-wt.html step 2; the mock's longer placeholder line sits in the field's tip (UX-PATTERNS §4).
Pictures were taken with the window behind another app, so the Create and Ask buttons show their background look.
